newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees Q4 actions sparking rebound.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees Q4 actions sparking rebound.

text.p: Motorola Inc said on Friday that cost cutting and other actions taken in the 1996 fourth quarter are designed spark a rebound in earnings growth in 1997 for the technology giant.

Motorola also said that it has begun to see a sequential quarterly increase in orders and sales as the worldwide semiconductor industry enters a cyclical rebound, though improved year-over-year financial results may not be evident until later in 1997.
Sales of semiconductor products accounted for 29 percent of Motorola's 1995 sales.

"We have initiated a reinvigorated process of discontinuing those development programs that have not lived up to their promise, further reducing costs in existing businesses that are not achieving adequate profitability, and refocusing our investments where we possess, or are cultivating, leadership core competencies," said Christopher Galvin, chief executive officer, in a statement.

"Motorola's Semiconductor Products Sector has begun to experience a sequential quarterly increase in orders and sales as the worldwide semiconductor industry enters a cyclical rebound, though improved year-over-year financial results may not be evident until later in 1997," he said.

"We expect only gradual sequential improvement in semiconductor sales and earnings during the first stages of the industry recovery. The long-term outlook for our communications businesses is as promising as ever; however, many of the factors that affected certain of our businesses should continue to have an adverse impact in early 1997," he said.

Looking at international markets, Galvin said the global economic outlook is healthy, "especially in emerging markets where Motorola is investing heavily, such as Latin America and Asia. We see balanced growth in the developed world as well."

Motorola reported 1996 fourth quarter earnings declined to $238 million or $0.39 a share on sales of about $7.69 billion. In the year ago quarter, the company reported earnings of $432 million or $0.72 a share on sales of about $7.30 billion.

Motorola said its 1996 fourth quarter earnings include "tens of millions of dollars" from cost cutting and restructuring actions including layoffs in the semiconductor business and other operations, some asset writedowns and decisions to end certain technology development programs.
Motorola said its 1996 fourth quarter sales of semiconductor products fell 18 percent to $1.9 billion, orders declined 11 percent, and the segment had an operating loss versus a profit a year ago.

Orders for semiconductors were lower in all regions compared with the fourth quarter of 1995. However, compared with the third quarter of 1996, orders improved in all regions, as well as most market segments and distribution, Motorola said.
